title: Conjecture 1
statement_text: There exists a constant $c > 1$ such that every $n$-vertex triangle-free planar graph has at least $c^{n^{\log_{9/2} 3}}$ distinct proper 3-colorings.
context_text: By Grötzsch's theorem every triangle-free planar graph is 3-colorable. Thomassen conjectured that such graphs have exponentially many proper 3-colorings, and proved that every $n$-vertex triangle-free planar graph has at least $c^{n^{1/12}}$ of them for some constant $c>1$; he later disproved his exponential conjecture by exhibiting, for infinitely many $n$, $n$-vertex triangle-free planar graphs with at most $2^{15n/\log_2 n}$ 3-colorings. The authors improve this construction: for infinitely many $n$ there is an $n$-vertex triangle-free planar graph with at most $64^{n^{\log_{9/2} 3}}<64^{n^{0.731}}$ proper 3-colorings. Since it does not seem possible to improve the exponent $\log_{9/2}3\approx 0.731$ with the same method, they conjecture that this exponent is optimal, which is the matching lower bound stated here.
notes: PDF source — the exponent 'nlog9/23' in the raw extraction is read as $n^{\log_{9/2} 3}$, consistent with the stated numerical approximation $n^{0.731}$ and the analytic derivation in the proof.
paper_title: Triangle-free planar graphs with at most $64^{n^{0.731}}$ 3-colorings
